CURRENT_HP.note: jag::opcode::get_npc_stat reads the current-stat and max-stat int[7] bases at a CS2-supplied index, and the NPC extended-info processor writes both from 24-bit wire levels at a wire-supplied index. HP is element 3, hence base+0xC. Not anchorable on this host: MSVC folds the index into the load's SIB and the recipe matcher cannot read a displacement out of an indexed operand. Index-3-is-hitpoints is inherited from standard stat ordering, so HIGH rather than CERTAIN - no 949-5 callsite pins it and the CS2 dumps have no npc_stat caller.

VTABLE.note: The manager is dispatched virtually as (**(code**)(*mgr + 8))(mgr,...) from the per-cycle update at 0x00027520, so offset 0 holds the vtable pointer. Derived on the PE independently of the ELF: the MAP_ANIM/spotanim packet handler at 0x0018b410 passes the manager (Client+0x19948) to the manager's Add at 0x0019e6c0, whose body is the whole evidence base for this cluster. Byte signatures do not port GCC->MSVC, so nothing here was carried from the Linux table.

POOL_FREE_LIST_HEAD.note: Node pool is based at manager+0x20. The allocate-or-recycle helper (ELF 0x129780, called from SpotAnimManager::Add@0x16a060 via LEA RDI,[RBX+0x20]; PE Add@0x19e6c0 identical) reads exactly four words: pool+0x00 free-list head, pool+0x08 bump cursor, pool+0x10 bump limit, pool+0x18 element stride = manager-relative 0x20/0x28/0x30/0x38, identical on both builds. Replaces the POOL_START/POOL_END pair, which had no correct binding: the allocator is a free-list plus a bump allocator, not a start/end pair. Surrounding fields corroborate the shared layout: head 0x10, tail 0x18, size 0x50 on both platforms.

SLOT_ARRAY.note: Slot array on the HintTrailList. jag::PacketHandlers::HintTrail indexes it with a scale-8 operand whose displacement the recipe matcher cannot be made to constrain, which is why the anchor that used to derive it is parked; established by hand against this build instead.

SLOT_COUNT.note: per-tick sweep@0x0018e7f6 MOV RCX,[client+0x198b8] (=OClient.HINTTRAIL_LIST) then LEA RBX,[RCX+0x10] / LEA RDI,[RCX+0x50]; 0x50-0x10=0x40=8*8. Both bounds are compile-time LEA immediates, not memory loads. Sibling list at client+0x198b0 has the identical layout.

ID.note: First member of the AnimationWrapper, copied straight out of the animation type at type+0x8 by jag::game::AnimationWrapper::Create, which pool-allocates a 0x68-byte control block, publishes the object at ctrl+0x20 and writes id, the type shared_ptr, the playback state and the -1 frame cursor in one run. Offset 0 carries no displacement for a recipe to capture, so it cannot be anchored; the Create sites are ELF 0x685e10 and PE 0x2f2890.

CLIENT.note: jag::ClientProt::FlushPerTick @0x1112c0: reaches the Client through [clientProt+0x8] on every branch and drives the senders as FlushMouseProtSender(clientProt+0x10) then FlushMouseProtSender(clientProt+0x38). Small fixed members of the ClientProt aggregate with no distinctive encoding of their own; the sender pair is emitted as two plain LEA arguments that a recipe cannot tell apart from any other LEA in a function that large.

KEY_ID.note: KeyEvent is a standard-layout scalar aggregate. Its stride and its three wire-visible members are pinned on this build - stride 0x20 from the vector push-back's 32-byte copy and its >>5/<<5 growth arithmetic, id at +0x0, repeat at +0xc and timestamp at +0x18 from jag::ClientProt::FlushPerTick's emit loop - which fixes the three purely local members between them at +0x4, +0x8 and +0x10 in declaration order, with +0x14 padding out to the 8-byte timestamp. Nothing here has a distinctive enough encoding for a recipe.
